options.C: Direct link between breach and injury
options.D: Actual injury or damage to the patient

explanation: Remember, negligence is about carelessness or mistakes, not a deliberate plot to hurt someone. You don't need malicious intent for negligence to occur!

question: Why is anticipating future needs an important part of nursing care in degenerative conditions?

options.A: It stops the genetic disorder from spreading to family members
options.B: It allows the team to prepare equipment and home changes before skills are lost
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will regain full mobility
options.D: It removes the need for ongoing nursing assessments

explanation: Thinking ahead means assistive devices and home changes can be arranged proactively, reducing stress and avoiding last-minute crises. Brilliant thinking!

question: Which behavior strongly suggests that a patient is dealing with high emotional stress?

options.A: Slow, deep, and regular breathing
options.B: Withdrawal and tearfulness
options.C: Eager participation in daily planning
options.D: Relaxed facial muscles and posture

explanation: When people feel overwhelmed emotionally, they often shut down, pull away from others, or break down in tears. Keep an eye out for these cues as a nurse! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why did health experts lower the amount of sugar in the standard ORS formula over time?

options.A: To save manufacturing costs for pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To make the powder dissolve faster in contaminated water
options.C: To stop children from developing diabetes during illness
options.D: To prevent excess sugar from pulling extra water back into the gut

explanation: Too much sugar actually acts like a sponge, drawing water back out into the stool. Lowering the sugar keeps the fluid moving safely into the body instead!

question: A new mum is worried about being very forgetful two weeks after giving birth. What should you do?

options.A: Refer her immediately for a complex magnetic resonance imaging scan of the brain
options.B: Notify the primary physician that she is showing signs of early-onset dementia
options.C: Instruct her to stop breastfeeding immediately to restore normal vitamin levels
options.D: Reassure her that temporary cognitive shifts and memory lapses are normal adaptive changes

explanation: Be her comfort! Postpartum 'brain fog' is totally normal as the brain adjusts. Reassuring her goes a long way in easing her anxiety.

question: Which of these is a very common nutrition challenge during the teenage years?

options.A: Development of eating disorders and poor dietary choices
options.B: Complete lack of appetite caused by hormonal stabilization
options.C: Permanent intolerance to all dairy calcium sources
options.D: Inability to absorb basic proteins from food

explanation: Between body image worries and busy school schedules, teens are extra vulnerable to skipping meals, picking junk food, or struggling with eating habits.

question: Why do nurses routinely check a urine sample (urinalysis) when evaluating new urine leaks?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To screen for prostate cancer markers
options.D: To measure exact kidney filtration rates

explanation: Infections can irritate the bladder and cause sudden leaks. Ruling out an infection is always a smart first step in nursing assessment.

question: At what point in an illness can a patient usually start receiving palliative care?

options.A: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.B: At the time of a serious illness diagnosis
options.C: Only when admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.D: After all curative treatments have completely failed

explanation: You don't have to wait until the end! Palliative care is meant to start early alongside other treatments to keep the patient as comfortable as possible.

question: How does benzonatate work to stop a patient's cough?

options.A: Anesthetizing stretch receptors in the respiratory tract
options.B: Depressing the heart rate to lower blood pressure
options.C: Paralyzing the muscles of the abdominal wall
options.D: Blocking histamine receptors in the nasal passages

explanation: Benzonatate acts locally by gently numbing the stretch receptors in the airways, stopping the urge to cough right at the source.

question: An elderly patient has thinning skin and less fat under the skin. What is the most important nursing care?

options.A: Applying heavy makeup to cover up skin discoloration
options.B: Encouraging vigorous daily scrubbing during baths
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Turning the patient regularly to prevent pressure sores

explanation: Brilliant! Without that cushioning layer of fat, older patients easily develop pressure sores, so helping them change positions regularly is key to keeping their skin safe.

question: How do large conferences usually differ from smaller seminars in nursing education?

options.A: Seminars always last for an entire week while conferences last only one hour.
options.B: Seminars focus exclusively on international health policies rather than clinical work.
options.C: Conferences are larger gatherings covering broad trends and offering networking opportunities.
options.D: Conferences are strictly hands-on practical sessions held in small hospital rooms.

explanation: Think of a conference as a big gathering where nurses from all over meet to share big ideas and research, while seminars are smaller, cozy deep-dives into specific topics.

question: Which leadership style is most appropriate during a sudden cardiac arrest emergency?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Delegative
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: An emergency requires fast, clear, direct instructions without debates, making autocratic leadership essential. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: A patient takes double their prescribed pain medication to get fast relief for a toothache. What is this called?

options.A: Casual substance use
options.B: Substance misuse
options.C: Normal recovery process
options.D: True physical addiction

explanation: Misuse simply means using a medication in a way other than how it was prescribed—like taking an extra dose on your own. Keep up the good work!

question: Why do health organizations strongly oppose 'medicalization'—which is performing FGM in a clinic by trained health workers?

options.A: It always causes immediate death from surgical shock
options.B: It increases the cost of healthcare services for the government
options.C: It prevents doctors from treating other common diseases
options.D: It validates and perpetuates a human rights violation rather than stopping it

explanation: Well reasoned! Doing FGM in a clinic gives a harmful practice fake medical approval instead of tackling the root gender inequality and abuse.

question: What must patients always drink plenty of when taking bulk-forming purgatives?

options.A: Concentrated protein shakes
options.B: Water and other fluids
options.C: High-fat dairy products
options.D: Acidic fruit juices

explanation: Always remember this clinical pearl: bulk-forming drugs need lots of water to expand safely, otherwise they can cause a blockage!

question: How do fake or substandard drugs make pharmacovigilance harder in places like Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate the need for healthcare workers to monitor patients
options.B: They ensure that all adverse drug reactions are automatically reported to NAFDAC
options.C: They introduce unpredictable toxicities and therapeutic failures that distort safety data
options.D: They make clinical trials completely unnecessary for pharmaceutical companies

explanation: You got it! Counterfeit drugs cause weird reactions or simply fail to work, which completely throws off our tracking of how safe real medicines are.

question: Which healthcare professional specializes in testing hearing and fitting hearing aids?

options.A: Ophthalmologist
options.B: Audiologist
options.C: Dietitian
options.D: Podiatrist

explanation: An audiologist is the expert you call for hearing tests, ear diagnoses, and finding the right hearing devices for patients. Easy to remember!

question: What is the term for the crunching or grinding sensation produced by broken bone ends rubbing together?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Contracture
options.C: Clonus
options.D: Crepitus

explanation: Crepitus occurs when jagged ends of a broken bone move against each other, creating a distinct grinding feel or sound. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h5)

question: How do nursing interventions help restore balance in a sick patient?

options.A: By stopping the patient from eating or drinking
options.B: By supporting or taking over failing regulatory systems
options.C: By replacing all natural body organs with machines
options.D: By curing viral infections without the use of drugs

explanation: Exactly right! As a nurse, you step in to help with breathing, hydration, or circulation whenever the patient's body needs backup.

question: Which organ failure leads directly to a dangerous buildup of water-soluble drugs in the body?

options.A: Pancreatic failure
options.B: Thyroid failure
options.C: Stomach failure
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Remember, the kidneys are our body's primary filtration filters for water-soluble waste and drugs. When they fail, those medications accumulate fast. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why do large arteries possess thick walls rich in elastic tissue?

options.A: To allow rapid diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide across the vessel wall
options.B: To store extra white blood cells during a systemic bacterial infection
options.C: To trap blood clots before they reach smaller vessels in the brain
options.D: To withstand and buffer the high-pressure surges of blood coming directly from the heart

explanation: The high elasticity of large arteries helps them absorb the forceful pulses of blood pumped by the heart, smoothing out pressure fluctuations. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community risk factor assessment for NCDs?

options.A: To penalize local food vendors who sell cheap processed carbohydrate meals
options.B: To secure international funding grants for building specialized cardiac hospitals
options.C: To gather local data and identify specific health needs before planning interventions
options.D: To diagnose individual patients with hypertension during routine house calls

explanation: Spot on! You can't solve a problem until you understand it. Assessing the community helps you design programs that actually fit their real-life struggles.

question: Why must you write down any recent antibiotics the patient is taking on the lab request form?

options.A: The laboratory requires proof that the prescription was filled
options.B: Medications can affect microbial growth and test interpretation
options.C: Pharmacies will not process the sample without this record
options.D: It determines the financial cost billed to the patient

explanation: Antibiotics in the patient's system can stop germs from growing in the lab dish, so the lab needs to know so they don't misread a false negative!

question: A patient wants an IUD right after an uncomplicated surgical abortion. What is the standard clinical practice?

options.A: She must wait for two normal menstrual periods
options.B: It can be safely inserted right away if there is no sign of infection
options.C: IUDs are never recommended after pregnancy termination
options.D: She must wait six weeks for her uterus to shrink

explanation: As long as there's no infection or trauma, an IUD can be placed immediately after the procedure. Saves the patient an extra trip!

question: What is the term for the grating sound heard when broken bone ends rub together?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Contracture
options.C: Crepitus
options.D: Clonus

explanation: Crepitus is the distinctive crunchy sound or sensation produced when rough ends of fractured bone rub together. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: What major public health threat is directly worsened by the over-prescription of antibiotics?

options.A: High blood pressure rates
options.B: Chronic kidney stone disease
options.C: Antimicrobial resistance
options.D: Nutritional vitamin deficiencies

explanation: Unnecessary antibiotic use teaches bacteria how to survive drug treatments, creating resistant strains that are hard to cure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: A patient with chest pain is awake and chatting with you in the clinic. Why should you NOT put an AED on them?

options.A: Chest pain medication must be given before applying any emergency electronic device.
options.B: The device only delivers shocks to patients who are unresponsive and in cardiac arrest.
options.C: The AED will automatically call emergency services if turned on near a living person.
options.D: The AED battery will drain too quickly if used on a conscious patient.

explanation: AEDs are smart! They check the heart rhythm and will only give a shock if a dangerous, shockable rhythm is found. If a patient is awake and breathing, the AED won't do anything—and they don't need one.

question: Which muscle does most of the heavy lifting when you take a normal, quiet breath in?

options.A: Internal intercostals
options.B: Sternocleidomastoid
options.C: Rectus abdominis
options.D: Diaphragm

explanation: Correct! The dome-shaped diaphragm is your main breathing muscle, moving down to pull air into your chest effortlessly.

question: If someone has a metabolic acid-base problem, which organ system jumps in first to try and balance it out?

options.A: The respiratory system through changes in ventilation
options.B: The integumentary system through sweat production
options.C: The digestive system through gastric acid secretion
options.D: The endocrine system through hormone release

explanation: Your lungs are fast responders! By breathing faster or slower, they can blow off or trap carbon dioxide to help fix metabolic imbalances quickly.

question: How do daily tally sheets make your life easier during busy clinic shifts?

options.A: By providing quick tick marks that save time during monthly summaries
options.B: By automatically ordering new contraceptive drugs from the depot
options.C: By replacing the need to ever write in the client register
options.D: By diagnosing common side effects of hormonal contraceptives

explanation: Exactly! Tally sheets let you mark services as you go, saving you from a massive headache at the end of the month.

question: You gently pinch an elderly patient's forearm skin and notice it stays tented up for a few seconds before going down. What does this mean?

options.A: Dehydration or reduced skin elasticity
options.B: Excessive fluid retention in the subcutaneous tissue
options.C: Severe local skin inflammation or infection
options.D: Normal physiological response to warm ambient air

explanation: When skin stays up after pinching (poor turgor), it's a classic sign of low fluid levels (dehydration) or normal aging changes.

question: Why was the team nursing model originally introduced in healthcare settings?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for registered nurses
options.B: To cope with nursing shortages and use various staff skills efficiently
options.C: To make patients pay less money for hospital admission
options.D: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Team nursing was designed to make the best use of available hands when professional nurses are limited in number. It's all about smart teamwork!

question: Which specific cells are responsible for producing protective mucus in the intestinal lining?

options.A: Goblet cells
options.B: G-cells
options.C: Parietal cells
options.D: Chief cells

explanation: Goblet cells secrete mucus that coats the intestinal lining, shielding it from friction and corrosive digestive juices. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is a frequent risk when people try to self-medicate ongoing, untreated anxiety?

options.A: Substance abuse and dependence
options.B: Sudden permanent loss of vision
options.C: Drastic and rapid skeletal bone growth
options.D: Complete immunity to bacterial infections

explanation: Spot on. Many turn to alcohol or drugs to numb their anxious feelings, which often leads into a struggle with substance dependence.

question: What does the term 'reliability' mean in the context of data collection?

options.A: Getting consistent results if the measurement is repeated
options.B: Collecting information quickly during an emergency
options.C: Storing physical records in a secure steel cabinet
options.D: Ensuring the data matches the exact true value

explanation: Reliability refers to the stability and consistency of data collection tools and methods over multiple uses. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h4)

question: What good daily habit should nurses encourage patients to practice regarding bowel movements?

options.A: Waiting until the weekend to try passing stool
options.B: Responding promptly to the natural urge to defecate
options.C: Holding bowel movements until bedtime
options.D: Straining forcefully every morning regardless of urge

explanation: You've got this! Ignoring the call of nature lets the colon suck out more water, making the stool much harder to pass later.

question: Why is preventing hypothermia especially important in a severely injured trauma patient?

options.A: It prevents the hospital room air conditioner from freezing
options.B: Warm patients require fewer intravenous fluids during surgery
options.C: Cold body temperatures can interfere with normal blood clotting
options.D: Hypothermia stops the patient from feeling any physical pain

explanation: Hypothermia is part of the lethal triad in trauma because it worsens bleeding by impairing the coagulation cascade. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why do people often get confused by the word 'stress' in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: They believe it is caused by mental exhaustion
options.B: They assume it only happens during high-intensity sports
options.C: They confuse it with neurological distress
options.D: They think it relates to emotional anxiety rather than physical pressure

explanation: It's an easy mix-up! In this case, 'stress' means physical force or pressure on your organs, not emotional stress or worry.

question: Why is In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) often suggested for patients with damaged or very short fallopian tubes?

options.A: It lengthens the existing tube through hormone stimulation
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying pelvic infections
options.C: It prevents ovulation from happening on the damaged side
options.D: It completely bypasses the need for functional fallopian tubes

explanation: With IVF, fertilization happens in a lab, and the embryo is placed straight into the uterus—meaning healthy fallopian tubes aren't needed at all!

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

options.A: To keep the operating room temperature from rising too high
options.B: To ensure the surgeon can see the blood vessels more clearly
options.C: To remove toxic smoke plumes and viral particles from the air
options.D: To prevent the fire alarm system from going off in the hospital

explanation: Electrical surgical tools create smoke containing harmful chemicals and tiny biological particles that theatre staff shouldn't breathe in.

question: How do normal proto-oncogenes cause trouble when they mutate?

options.A: They permanently shut down all cellular activity in the organ
options.B: They cause the immune system to destroy healthy tissue
options.C: They stop the tumor from getting a blood supply
options.D: They become overactive oncogenes that drive constant cell division

explanation: Spot on! When proto-oncogenes mutate, they turn into hyperactive oncogenes that act like a stuck accelerator pedal, shouting for the cell to multiply nonstop.

question: A patient is brought in with no breathing and no pulse. What quick physical check confirms cardiac arrest?

options.A: Checking the skin color on the hands and feet
options.B: Measuring the blood pressure using an automated cuff
options.C: Testing the deep tendon reflexes in the knees
options.D: Auscultating the chest with a stethoscope for heart sounds

explanation: You got it! Listening directly to the chest with your stethoscope is a reliable way to check if heart sounds are completely gone.

question: Which structures are removed during a standard Type II FGM procedure?

options.A: The clitoris and the labia minora
options.B: The entire vulva and perineum
options.C: Only the pubic hair follicles
options.D: Only the vaginal mucous membrane

explanation: Type II goes a step further than Type I by removing both the clitoris and the labia minora (sometimes along with parts of the labia majora).

question: Which condition is linked directly to hypothalamic damage that messes up fluid balance?

options.A: Diabetes insipidus
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Chronic insomnia
options.D: Hemiballismus

explanation: Well done! When the hypothalamus or posterior pituitary is damaged, anti-diuretic hormone drops, causing the massive water loss seen in diabetes insipidus.

question: What is the main idea behind interdisciplinary collaboration in healthcare?

options.A: Hospital management handling budgets without input from clinicians
options.B: Doctors making all patient care decisions without consulting others
options.C: Nurses working entirely independently within their specific wards
options.D: Professionals from different health fields working together for a patient

explanation: You've got this! Interdisciplinary collaboration simply means bringing different health experts together to combine their unique skills for the best patient outcome.

question: At what age group are public health programs primarily targeting the HPV vaccine for the best results?

options.A: Pre-adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years
options.B: Infants during their routine immunization schedule
options.C: Adult women over the age of 50 years
options.D: Pregnant women during prenatal clinic visits

explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine works best when given before any exposure to the virus through sexual activity, which is why pre-teens aged 9 to 14 are the main target group.

question: A junior nurse sees a mother bleeding heavily after birth but stays quiet because she is scared of the senior doctor. What kind of barrier is this?

options.A: Hierarchical barrier
options.B: Equipment failure
options.C: Alert fatigue
options.D: Confirmation bias

explanation: Spot on. Strict hospital ranks can make junior staff too intimidated to speak up. Patient safety means every voice matters, no matter your rank!

question: Why do nurses study anatomy and physiology together?

options.A: Pathology cannot occur without simultaneous changes in both areas
options.B: How an organ is built directly shapes how it does its job
options.C: Medical equipment is built based strictly on anatomical dimensions
options.D: It is a strict requirement for passing hospital licensing exams

explanation: You've got this! Structure and function always go hand in hand. An organ's physical shape is specially designed to make its everyday job possible. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: How long must a seizure continue for it to be called status epilepticus?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: Longer than 5 minutes
options.C: At least 60 minutes
options.D: More than 2 hours

explanation: A seizure lasting past five minutes—or happening back-to-back without waking up—is status epilepticus. It's a true medical emergency!

question: When would a nurse use the intraosseous (IO) route for giving fluids?

options.A: As the routine first choice for every patient needing oral medication
options.B: When the patient refuses to take medications by mouth
options.C: When peripheral veins cannot be accessed quickly in a severe shock emergency
options.D: Only after the patient has fully recovered and is ready for discharge

explanation: When shock hits and veins collapse, going straight into the bone marrow (IO) is a lifesaver for getting fluids in fast.

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's bedside locker to clear out old, forgotten food brought by family?

options.A: Perishable foods lose all their carbohydrate value within two hours
options.B: Hospital policy forbids patients from eating food brought by relatives
options.C: Unrefrigerated perishable food breeds bacteria that cause food poisoning
options.D: Non-perishable items attract insects if left near hospital beds

explanation: You got it! Sick patients have weaker immune systems, so warm food sitting in a locker can quickly grow dangerous bacteria and cause tummy trouble.

question: Why is it so important to follow a specific journal's instructions before submitting your paper?

options.A: It eliminates any need to report study limitations in the discussion
options.B: It guarantees that the journal will publish the paper without peer review
options.C: It prevents immediate rejection due to formatting or scope mismatches
options.D: It reduces the total word count of the study to under fifty words

explanation: Right! Journals get tons of papers and will often reject them instantly if they don't follow basic formatting and topic guidelines.

question: You test fluid pulled from a newly placed NG tube and find a pH of 4.0. What does this tell you?

options.A: The patient is experiencing severe lung infection.
options.B: The tube is correctly placed in the stomach.
options.C: The tube is coiled inside the patient's esophagus.
options.D: The tube has accidentally entered the lungs.

explanation: Stomach acid is nice and acidic, usually sitting between pH 1.0 and 5.5. A pH of 4.0 is a great sign you are in the right spot!

question: A patient just lost her home in a fire. She won't eat, stares at the wall, and speaks in whispers. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge her since she has no bleeding wounds
options.B: Tell her things could have been much worse
options.C: Check her immediate physical safety and basic comfort needs
options.D: Leave her alone so she can sit in total silence

explanation: Safety and basic physiological needs always come first when someone has just gone through severe shock and trauma.

question: What does the term 'bioavailability' mean when studying nutrition?

options.A: The expiration date stamped on a packaged food item
options.B: The speed at which bacteria break down food in the large intestine
options.C: The fraction of an ingested nutrient that enters the bloodstream and becomes active
options.D: The total percentage of water found inside a raw vegetable

explanation: Exactly right! Bioavailability simply means how much of the nutrient successfully makes it past your gut and into your bloodstream to go to work.

question: Why is early recognition of occupational lung diseases so critical for patients?

options.A: Treatment only works during the first week of coughing
options.B: The lung tissue scarring is usually permanent once it forms
options.C: Employers will immediately pay compensation before it spreads
options.D: Infections will spread to the brain within a few hours

explanation: Because the damage caused by dust accumulation leads to irreversible fibrosis, catching the condition early helps prevent further exposure and worsening illness. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: What should you do if an old gauze dressing is stuck tightly to a healing wound?

options.A: Leave the old gauze stuck and put new dressings on top.
options.B: Moisten it gently with sterile normal saline to loosen it.
options.C: Soak the whole patient in hot soapy water.
options.D: Rip it off quickly with a fast jerk to save time.

explanation: Never rip dry gauze off! A little sterile saline softens the dried fluid and protects that precious new skin underneath.

question: Why are pregnant women advised to drink fluids between meals rather than during meals?

options.A: To keep stomach acid completely inactive during digestion
options.B: To prevent over-stretching the stomach which can trigger vomiting
options.C: To ensure the body absorbs all the vitamins from the solid food
options.D: To stop the kidneys from working too hard after eating

explanation: Filling the stomach with both food and large amounts of liquid at the same time increases pressure and promotes vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: Why is a low blood albumin level usually a sign of long-standing (chronic) liver trouble rather than a sudden issue?

options.A: Albumin is stored in large amounts in fat tissue before being released
options.B: Acute liver injury causes albumin to temporarily hide inside the kidneys
options.C: Albumin has a long half-life, so levels drop slowly over weeks of poor production
options.D: The body stops producing red blood cells before it stops making albumin

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Because albumin stays in circulation for about three weeks, it takes a while of poor liver production for levels to noticeably crash.

question: Which tool is commonly used with a penlight to check the front part of the nose?

options.A: Ophthalmoscope
options.B: Nasal speculum
options.C: Laryngoscope
options.D: Tympanometer

explanation: A nasal speculum gently opens up the nostril so you can easily inspect the inside lining and nasal septum.

question: What is the main purpose of using a genogram during a family nursing assessment?

options.A: To calculate the exact monthly income of the household
options.B: To track the daily caloric intake of the patient
options.C: To list all community parks near the patient's home
options.D: To map out inherited medical conditions across generations

explanation: A genogram acts as a detailed family tree that helps nurses identify hereditary health risks and family patterns. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of public health surveillance systems during an infectious disease threat?

options.A: To calculate the annual financial profits of private clinics
options.B: To punish hospitals that fail to meet administrative standards
options.C: To restrict all international trade between neighboring nations
options.D: To detect, track, and report unusual disease outbreaks quickly

explanation: Surveillance monitors disease patterns so health agencies can spot outbreaks early and take action to protect the public. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h9)

question: Why is it important for a nurse educator to know and use more than one teaching method?

options.A: Hospital management mandates a change of method every single week
options.B: Different learning objectives and situations require different instructional approaches
options.C: Using multiple methods is the only way to assign passing grades
options.D: Students lose their nursing license if they experience only one teaching style

explanation: Just like you wouldn't use the same nursing procedure for every patient, you can't teach anatomy theory the exact same way you teach emergency resuscitation skills. Variety helps concepts stick!

question: Which healthcare professional frequently acts as the central coordinator within a multidisciplinary care team for chronic degenerative conditions?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The surgical technician
options.C: The registered nurse
options.D: The billing administrator

explanation: Nurses coordinate day-to-day care and communicate patient needs across various medical specialists and therapists. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h6)

question: Why do patients sometimes feel tummy pain during the early stage of this infection?

options.A: Adult worms multiply inside the lower digestive tract
options.B: Toxins from the lung flukes specifically target the stomach lining
options.C: Juvenile worms burrow through the intestinal wall and belly lining
options.D: Bad bacteria grow from eating contaminated food

explanation: You got it! Once the baby flukes hatch in the gut, they have to crawl right through the gut wall and up toward the lungs, causing some local irritation along the way.

question: What kind of mask do you need when entering a patient's room who is on droplet precautions?

options.A: No mask is ever required
options.B: A cloth fashion face covering
options.C: A powered air-purifying respirator
options.D: A standard surgical mask

explanation: For droplet precautions, a standard surgical mask is all you need to block those larger splashes and secretions.

question: How should a freshly applied Plaster of Paris cast be supported while it dries?

options.A: Covered tightly with heavy warm blankets to trap heat
options.B: Suspended vertically by a rope attached to the ceiling
options.C: Lying directly flat on a hard wooden examination table
options.D: Resting on soft pillows with open air circulation

explanation: Soft pillows cradle the wet cast and support its shape without pressing flat, damaging spots into the drying plaster.

question: What do we call the tiny, milk-producing sacs found inside the breast lobules?

options.A: Alveoli
options.B: Montgomery's tubercles
options.C: Myoepithelial cells
options.D: Lactiferous sinuses

explanation: Think of alveoli as the little factories where breast milk is actually made! They are clustered together inside the breast lobules. You've got this!

question: Why are degenerative neurological disorders considered irreversible?

options.A: Neurons cannot easily regenerate once destroyed
options.B: Blood flow to the brain stops completely
options.C: Treatments are never started early enough
options.D: The immune system constantly attacks the brain

explanation: Once nerve cells in the central nervous system are lost, the body cannot easily replace them, leading to permanent structural decline. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h1)

question: A care assistant is about to feed a resident who has trouble swallowing. What safety tip should you give?

options.A: Offer large chunks of solid food for better chewing
options.B: Feed the resident as quickly as possible
options.C: Position the resident in an upright sitting posture
options.D: Encourage the resident to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to help swallowing and keeps food out of the lungs, preventing dangerous choking.

question: Why do you need to check a patient's medication list before they get an EMG test?

options.A: To ensure the patient has taken their daily antibiotics
options.B: To prevent allergic reactions to the conductive gel used
options.C: To stop pain medications that would numb the skin entirely
options.D: To check for drugs that thin the blood and risk bleeding

explanation: Because an EMG involves placing thin needles directly into muscle tissue, taking blood thinners can put the patient at risk for internal bleeding or hematomas.

question: If a patient has severe kidney failure, what adjustment would a nurse expect for a drug that is normally cleared by the kidneys?

options.A: Stopping all fluid intake to prevent the drug from diluting in the blood
options.B: Switching the patient immediately to a heavy lipid-soluble oral syrup
options.C: A reduction in the drug dose or an increased time interval between doses
options.D: Giving a double dose to overcome the buildup of metabolic waste

explanation: When kidneys aren't working at full speed, drugs stick around much longer. Nurses must watch out for this and expect lower doses or spaced-out timing to keep patients safe from toxicity!

question: Which IV fluid is the only safe choice to use for priming blood tubing?

options.A: 0.45% Sodium Chloride
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: Ringer's Lactate Solution

explanation: Stick to Normal Saline (0.9%)! Dextrose can actually make red blood cells burst (hemolysis), and Ringer's Lactate has calcium that can cause the blood to clot in the tubing.

question: Why is it actually a good thing that the mother's blood and the baby's blood do not mix directly?

options.A: To keep the fetal body temperature lower than the mother's core temperature
options.B: To allow the placenta to produce hormones without interference
options.C: To prevent the mother's high blood pressure from damaging fragile fetal blood vessels
options.D: To stop the fetus from rejecting the mother's blood cells immediately

explanation: Spot on! Mother's blood pressure can be quite high, so keeping the bloodstreams separate protects the baby's tiny, delicate blood vessels from bursting.

question: When are transmission-based precautions added to patient care?

options.A: Only after laboratory tests prove the patient is cured
options.B: When the hospital runs out of standard gloves
options.C: When a specific contagious disease is suspected or confirmed
options.D: Whenever a visitor enters the isolation room

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are extra steps added on top of standard rules when dealing with specific, easily spread germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which drug history is most important for a nurse to check before a patient has a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Multivitamins
options.B: Antacids
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Anticoagulants

explanation: Spot on! Blood thinners (anticoagulants) raise the risk of dangerous bleeding around the spine.

question: A patient recovering from near-asphyxiation is cleared to eat, but struggles to swallow properly. Who should you consult?

options.A: A diagnostic radiologist
options.B: A speech-language pathologist
options.C: A hospital pharmacist
options.D: A physical fitness instructor

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at assessing and retraining swallowing safely, keeping patients safe from aspiration pneumonia. Teamwork makes the dream work in healthcare!

question: What does your skin do when you step into a cold environment?

options.A: Blood vessels in the skin widen to let heat out
options.B: Sweat glands release extra cooling fluid
options.C: Melanocytes produce more dark pigment
options.D: Blood vessels in the skin narrow to hold in body heat

explanation: Well done! When it's cold, your blood vessels squeeze shut near the surface to keep your warm blood safely around your inner organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why must the middle ear amplify sound vibrations before they pass into the inner ear?

options.A: Air molecules travel too fast for the cochlea to catch them
options.B: The brain cannot process low-amplitude sounds without assistance
options.C: Sound loses energy when moving from air into the fluid of the inner ear
options.D: The inner ear requires electrical current instead of physical movement

explanation: Sound waves tend to bounce off liquid surfaces. Because the inner ear is filled with fluid, the middle ear bones must boost the sound pressure so it doesn't get lost!

question: What is the main purpose of 'informed choice' in nursing practice?

options.A: Empowering clients to select a method voluntarily based on complete facts
options.B: Allowing the healthcare provider to make the final medical decision
options.C: Ensuring every clinic client uses the exact same long-acting method
options.D: Complying with hospital policies without listening to client preferences

explanation: Great thinking! Informed choice respects our clients' rights, making sure they pick a method freely based on honest and complete information, with zero pressure.

question: Which type of nerve fibers send those sharp, instant pain signals?

options.A: Ruffini fibers
options.B: Merkel fibers
options.C: C fibers
options.D: A-delta fibers

explanation: Brilliant! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin, which lets them rush electrical impulses quickly to cause that sharp first pain.

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment finds candidates, while selection chooses the best fit
options.B: Recruitment checks licenses, while selection checks exam scores
options.C: Selection is done by human resources, and recruitment is done by doctors
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

explanation: Recruitment brings people in to apply, and selection is the screening process used to pick the right hire. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is the involvement of traditional and religious leaders crucial when planning community health interventions?

options.A: They are legally required to sign every nurse's monthly salary voucher
options.B: They provide international grants for buying hospital equipment
options.C: They help build trust and dismantle cultural resistance among community members
options.D: They possess formal training in advanced surgical procedures

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold massive influence over local beliefs and behavior, making them key allies in overcoming health rumors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Why is community advocacy an essential responsibility for nurses dealing with forced marriage?

options.A: It helps challenge harmful traditions and prevents future cases through education
options.B: It allows nurses to act as judges in local community court systems
options.C: It replaces the need for direct clinical care inside hospital wards
options.D: It is the only way for hospitals to receive funding for medical supplies

explanation: Community advocacy raises awareness and shifts cultural attitudes, helping to protect potential victims before marriages occur. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h7)

question: How does poor food purchasing directly affect patient outcomes?

options.A: It improves the patient's appetite significantly
options.B: It always results in immediate food poisoning
options.C: It decreases the overall cost of hospital stays
options.D: It can lead to nutrient deficiencies and health complications

explanation: Sourcing poor quality or inadequate food items deprives the body of essential nutrients needed for recovery and maintenance. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.A: Complete disappearance of capillary beds
options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.C: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged valves
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults.
